event.text:
The Go test expects every canonical key to be in the report and match. So Go must output the same keys. The canonical has: aspect_ratio_xy, aspect_ratio_xz, aspect_ratio_yz, bounding_box_max, bounding_box_min, centroid, characteristic_length, convex_hull_volume, dimension_x, dimension_y, dimension_z, euler_characteristic, face_count, footprint_area, is_watertight, moments_of_inertia, principal_axes, slenderness, total_surface_area, vertex_count.

Go now has slenderness. But Go doesn't have convex_hull_volume, moments_of_inertia, principal_axes - and we're not implementing those in Go. So we have two options: (1) Remove those from canonical so all languages only output the common subset, or (2) Have Go output placeholder values for those (e.g. 0, empty array) and then the canonical would need to have those placeholder values for the "subset" of keys that Go produces - but then Python would output real values and the canonical would have real values, so Go would fail when comparing convex_hull_volume.

So the only way is: canonical contains only the keys that ALL languages can compute. So remove from canonical: convex_hull_volume, moments_of_inertia, principal_axes. Then Python's geometric_insights_to_report_dict can still output them (so Python report has more keys), but the canonical asset only has the common keys. Then every language test: build report with the keys that language computes; assert that for each key in canonical, key is in report and report[key] == canonical[key]. So we don't require report to have all canonical keys - we require canonical to be a subset of report and match. So actually: canonical is the set of keys we expect every language to produce. So we need to remove convex_hull_volume, moments_of_inertia, principal_axes from the canonical asset. Let me regenerate the canonical from Python but only include the keys that we'll implement in all languages: bounding_box_min, bounding_box_max, centroid, dimension_x/y/z, characteristic_length, footprint_area, total_surface_area, aspect_ratio_xy/xz/yz, slenderness, vertex_count, face_count, euler_characteristic, is_watertight. And optionally enclosed_volume, surface_to_volume if we add them in Go (Go has them). So canonical = subset of Python output without principal_axes, moments_of_inertia, convex_hull_volume. Let me update the Python reporter to optionally exclude those, then regenerate canonical. Or we could just delete those keys from the current canonical file. Let me do that - edit model-kpi-nakagin.json to remove "convex_hull_volume", "moments_of_inertia", "principal_axes". Then Go test: build report with Point as {x,y,z} (Go's Point serializes to {"X","Y","Z"} with caps - need to use json tags. Let me check Go Point struct.
